name: Operation Overlord
notes: Codename of the Allied invasion and campaign in north-west Europe. Wikipedia ends it at the German withdrawal across the Seine, 30 August 1944; some sources end it on 25 August. CMH has no Overlord streamer. An umbrella only: no claim after 30 August 1944 carries it as its operation (the derived operation_name is blank outside these dates), while the Northern France campaign continues to 14 September.

name: Normandy campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 6 June-24 July 1944. The streamer ends the day before Cobra opens (25 July); the first, aborted Cobra bombing was on 24 July.

name: Northern France campaign
parent_date_exception: CMH streamer runs to 14 September; Overlord (Wikipedia) ends 30 August. The campaign is a child of Overlord only for the days both cover; the derived operation_name stops on 30 August.
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 25 July-14 September 1944.

name: Southern France campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 15 August-14 September 1944. Overlaps Northern France by design; a row takes it only through its operation (Dragoon).

name: Rhineland campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 15 September 1944-21 March 1945. Overlaps Ardennes-Alsace; rows of the Ardennes fighting take Ardennes-Alsace through their operation, other rows Rhineland.

name: Ardennes-Alsace campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 16 December 1944-25 January 1945.

name: Central Europe campaign
notes: CMH campaign streamer, 22 March-11 May 1945. Reserved: no claim yet.

name: Operation Neptune
notes: The assault phase of Overlord: the amphibious invasion and the establishment of a foothold. The end date, 30 June 1944, is the date on which Neptune is said to have ended (Wikipedia, Beachhead); the Normandy landings article gives no end date. operation_places: added sourced Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno and Sword Beach landing_area rows with no primary_place_id (old value blank, left blank); reason: this operation is not reduced to a single pin (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Tonga
parent_date_exception: The drop began on the night of 5/6 June, before the 6 June start of Neptune and of the Normandy streamer.
notes: British 6th Airborne Division operation on the eastern flank, 5-7 June 1944 (Wikipedia).

name: Operation Perch
notes: British attempt to take Caen from the east, 7-14 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Operation Epsom
notes: British VIII Corps offensive west of Caen, 26-30 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Operation Martlet
notes: British XXX Corps flank operation, 25 June-1 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Carried out in support of Epsom (see data/operation_relations.csv).

name: Battle of Cherbourg
alt_names: Cotentin Peninsula operations; Capture of Cherbourg
notes: Wikipedia dates the Cotentin Peninsula operations 6 June-1 July 1944 and the fight for the city 22-27 June. This row takes the wider window because claims labelled Cherbourg include the VII Corps moves from the Utah landing (7 June) to the capture. Contested boundary: the narrow window would leave 18 earlier claims without this operation. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0089 (Cherbourg); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Cutting the Cotentin
notes: VII Corps attack across the base of the Cotentin to cut off the peninsula (Barneville reached 18 June). No source gives the phase a date range: the dates are the span of the narrative in Cross-Channel Attack ch. X and Utah Beach to Cherbourg ch. 8 as used for the five claims.

name: Battle of Carentan
notes: 10-14 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0067 (Carentan, Manche); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of Bloody Gulch
notes: 13 June 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); part of the fighting around Carentan.

name: Operation Cobra
notes: 25-31 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Placement: Cobra opened on 25 July, the first day of the Northern France streamer, so it is a child of Northern France, not Normandy (the first bombing, 24 July, was aborted). Decision for the owner if the planned date should count instead.

name: Brittany campaign
parent_date_exception: Ends 19 September with the end of the Brest fighting, after the Northern France streamer ends on 14 September; claims after 14 September take the Rhineland streamer by date.
notes: Third Army operations in Brittany from 1 August 1944 (Third Army operational, Breakout and Pursuit Part Four) to the end of the Brest fighting. Wikipedia gives only "August-September 1944"; the dates are set from the Green Book narrative. Contested.

name: Siege of Brest
notes: Wikipedia: 7 August-20 September 1944. Breakout and Pursuit: the battle ended on 18 September with the surrender of Brest; the Crozon peninsula was cleared on 19 September, which is the end date used. Contested boundary. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0045 (Brest, Finistère); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of Mortain
notes: The Allied side of the German counterattack toward Avranches, 7-13 August 1944. Wikipedia covers it under the German codename, Operation Lüttich. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0236 (Mortain, Manche); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Lüttich
notes: German name of the counterattack at Mortain, 7-13 August 1944. No claim points at this row: it records the German name and links to the Battle of Mortain.

name: Battle of the Falaise Pocket
notes: 12-21 August 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). operation_places: added sourced Falaise namesake and Falaise-pocket representative rows with no primary_place_id (old value blank, left blank); reason: this operation is not reduced to a single pin (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Liberation of Paris
notes: 19-25 August 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0271 (Paris); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Pursuit across France
notes: The drive from the Seine to the German border. No source dates it: the start is the Seine crossing (19 August, Breakout and Pursuit) and the end is the close of the Northern France streamer (14 September; The Siegfried Line Campaign opens on 11 September). Contested; claims labelled Pursuit before 19 August are not matched to it.

name: Operation Dragoon
notes: Allied landings in southern France and the advance up the Rhone valley, 15 August-14 September 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the same dates as the Southern France streamer.

name: Lorraine campaign
notes: Third Army operations in Lorraine, 1 September-18 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox; The Lorraine Campaign opens on 1 September). Spans the Northern France and Rhineland streamers, so it has no parent.

name: Siegfried Line campaign
notes: Wikipedia: 28 August-16 December 1944. The Green Book (The Siegfried Line Campaign) opens with the First Army on 11 September. Spans two streamers, so it has no parent. Contested start.

name: Battle of Aachen
parent_date_exception: Wikipedia dates the battle from 12 September, three days before the Rhineland streamer opens.
notes: 12 September-21 October 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the US assault on the city itself was 2-21 October. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0001 (Aachen, North Rhine-Westphalia); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of the Scheldt
notes: 2 October-8 November 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). operation_places: added sourced Antwerp, Walcheren, South Beveland, Breskens and Woensdrecht rows with no primary_place_id (old value blank, left blank); reason: this operation is not reduced to a single pin (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of the Vosges
notes: 15 September 1944-15 February 1945 (Wikipedia infobox, a wide span); the claims concern the October-November fighting described in The Riviera to the Rhine ch. 22.

name: Operation Queen
notes: First and Ninth Army offensive toward the Roer, 16 November-16 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Claims labelled Roer in the earlier dataset before 16 November are not matched to it.

name: Operation Clipper
notes: British XXX Corps and US 84th Division attack on Geilenkirchen, 10-22 November 1944 (Wikipedia infobox).

name: Operation Market Garden
notes: 17-25 September 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). operation_places: added sourced Arnhem, Nijmegen, Eindhoven, Oosterbeek and Veghel rows with no primary_place_id (old value blank, left blank); reason: this operation is not reduced to a single pin (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of the Bulge
parent_date_exception: Wikipedia ends the battle on 28 January 1945; the Ardennes-Alsace streamer ends on 25 January.
notes: 16 December 1944-28 January 1945 (Wikipedia infobox). Contested end date.

name: Operation Wacht am Rhein
notes: German codename of the Ardennes offensive. No claim points at this row; it records the German name and links to the Battle of the Bulge.

name: Siege of Bastogne
notes: 20-26 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the relief by Third Army reached the town on 26 December. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0031 (Bastogne, Luxembourg); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Nordwind
notes: 31 December 1944-25 January 1945 (Wikipedia). The German offensive in Alsace and Lorraine; the row serves the Allied defence of the Seventh Army front, as the Bulge row serves the Ardennes.

name: Colmar Pocket
notes: 20 January-9 February 1945 (Wikipedia infobox for the Allied reduction of the pocket); the German hold in central Alsace dates from November 1944. Spans the Ardennes-Alsace streamer (ends 25 January) and the Rhineland streamer, so no parent. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0403 (Colmar, Haut-Rhin); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Grenade
notes: 23 February-10 March 1945 (Wikipedia infobox); the Ninth Army crossing of the Roer to link with the Canadian First Army in Veritable. Wikipedia text also says 9 February for the original plan, postponed after the dams were flooded.

name: Battle of Remagen
notes: 7-25 March 1945 (Wikipedia: an 18-day battle). Spans the Rhineland streamer (ends 21 March) and the Central Europe streamer, so no parent. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0422 (Ludendorff Bridge, Remagen); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Undertone
notes: 8-24 March 1945 (Wikipedia infobox); the U.S. Seventh, Third and French First Armies. The Seventh Army attack began on 15 March (Last Offensive ch. 12 p. 253). Spans the Rhineland streamer (ends 21 March) and the Central Europe streamer, so no parent.

name: Operation Varsity
notes: 24 March 1945: the airborne landing east of the Rhine near Wesel (Wikipedia; Last Offensive ch. 14 p. 310 has the first flight over the target at 0953).

name: Ruhr pocket
alt_names: Reduction of the Ruhr pocket; Ruhr encirclement
notes: 1-18 April 1945: the encirclement of Army Group B in the Ruhr closed on 1 April (Last Offensive ch. 16 p. 359-362; Wikipedia: the lead elements of the two Allied army groups met on 1 April) and the First and Ninth Armies reduced the pocket from 4 April; organized resistance ended on 18 April (Last Offensive ch. 16 p. 372; Wikipedia, Ruhr pocket). Both give 18 April as the end; Wikipedia says the reduction began on 1 April with the Ninth Army, the Green Book (map 5) dates the reduction from 4 April, when the Ninth Army returned to the 12th Army Group; the operation starts on the date of the closing of the ring, which both sources give. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0640 (Ruhr pocket (representative point at Essen)); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Harz pocket
notes: 11-23 April 1945: the 1st Division pierced the western fringe of the Harz on 11 April and the Americans reduced the pocket in the mountains (Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 402-405); the Green Book map 6 is titled "The Harz Pocket 11-17 April 1945" and the fight ended on 23 April, when a patrol found the Eleventh Army command post near Blankenburg and captured the staff (p. 405). The end date is the 23 April of the text, not the 17 April of the map title; the source gives no start before 11 April.

name: Battle of Nuremberg (1945)
notes: 16-20 April 1945: the Seventh Army (XV Corps with the 3d and 45th Divisions) began its assault on the city on 16 April and the 3d Division's 30th Infantry entered the old town late on 19 April; the city fell on 20 April (Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 424-425; Wikipedia: a five-day battle, the Seventh Army took the city centre on 20 April). primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0476 (Nuremberg, Bayern); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Charnwood
notes: Anglo-Canadian I Corps offensive that took most of Caen north of the Orne, 8-9 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Added in German Batch 1b as context for the German units in the Caen sector. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0057 (Caen); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Jupiter
notes: British VIII Corps attack on Hill 112 and Maltot, 10-11 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox). Added in German Batch 1b as context for the 9th SS, 10th SS and 1st SS Panzer Divisions.

name: Operation Goodwood
notes: British VIII Corps offensive east of Caen, 18-20 July 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); Wikipedia dates the aftermath separately. Added in German Batch 1b as context for the German units east and south of Caen.

name: Battle of Metz
notes: 27 September-13 December 1944 (Wikipedia infobox); the city fell on 22 November and the last fort surrendered on 13 December. Added in German Batch 2 as a context record; no German-unit claim of Batch 2 is dated inside it. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0224 (Metz, Moselle); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of the Hürtgen Forest
notes: Window of the November-December 1944 fighting, set by the dataset authors from the Siegfried Line Green Book: H Hour of the 28th Division's attack toward Schmidt was 0900 on 2 November (ch. 15, p. 348), and on 14 December the 329th Infantry had put the Huertgen Forest behind and emerged on the Roer plain (ch. 25, p. 592). The Green Book's Part Five is titled The Huertgen Forest (chapters 16 to 20) and its chapter 4 covers a first fight in the forest in September, so the fighting began earlier, and the attack on the Roer dams (ch. 26) continued it; this record covers only the November-December fighting, the period of the German Batch 3 claims. Added in the German Batch 3 follow-up (28 October 2026). primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0586 (Hürtgen, North Rhine-Westphalia); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Battle of the Roer Plain
notes: 16 November-9 December 1944: Part Six of the Siegfried Line Green Book is titled Battle of the Roer Plain (chapters 21 to 24), and its Map VIII, Drive to the Roer, is dated 16 November-9 December 1944 (ch. 22). Child of Operation Queen (OP-QUEEN), whose dates run to 16 December; the Roer dams attack of 13-15 December (ch. 26) is not part of this record. Added in the German Batch 3 follow-up (28 October 2026).

name: Operation Atlantic
notes: II Canadian Corps attack south-east of Caen (Colombelles, Vaucelles, Louvigny, Verrieres Ridge), launched with Goodwood. Stacey (p. 171) gives D Day as 18 July and (p. 176) speaks of the operations of 18-21 July east of the Orne; the end date is the last day of that window. Added in Canadian Batch 1.

name: Operation Spring
notes: II Canadian Corps attack on Verrieres Ridge and Tilly-la-Campagne, D Day 25 July at 03:30 (Stacey p. 186); the further attack planned for 26 July was cancelled (p. 193), so the row covers 25 July only. Added in Canadian Batch 1.

name: Operation Totalize
notes: II Canadian Corps night attack down the Caen-Falaise road. The columns crossed the start line on the night of 7-8 August (start date 7 August); Stacey (p. 231) calls the operation at an end after the failed attack on Quesnay Wood on the evening of 10 August. Added in Canadian Batch 1.

name: Operation Wellhit
notes: 3rd Canadian Infantry Division assault on Boulogne: D Day 17 September (Stacey p. 338), ended on the afternoon of 22 September (p. 343). The parent is the campaign streamer that starts on 15 September. Added in Canadian Batch 1. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0677 (Boulogne-sur-Mer, Pas-de-Calais); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Undergo
notes: 3rd Canadian Infantry Division assault on Calais: attack at 10:15 on 25 September (Stacey p. 349), all resistance ended by 09:00 on 1 October (p. 352). Added in Canadian Batch 1. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0678 (Calais, Pas-de-Calais); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Switchback
notes: 3rd Canadian Infantry Division attack across the Leopold Canal and amphibious landing that cleared the Breskens pocket south of the West Scheldt: began early on 6 October (Stacey p. 393), declared complete at 09:50 on 3 November (p. 400). Added in Canadian Batch 1.

name: Operation Elephant
notes: 4th Canadian Armoured Division (10th Brigade) attack on the German bridgehead at Kapelsche Veer on the Oude Maasje island: launched on the morning of 26 January (Stacey p. 453); the Lincoln and Welland Regiment made contact with the Argylls early on the morning of 31 January and no Germans remained alive south of the main stream of the Maas (p. 454). Added in Canadian Batch 2. primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0715 (Kapelsche Veer, Noord-Brabant); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Veritable
alt_names: Battle of the Reichswald; Battle of the Rhineland (Canadian Army)
notes: First Canadian Army offensive between the Maas and the Rhine, opened early on 8 February (Stacey p. 467); the Army casualty period for the battle is 8 February to 10 March (p. 522). The end date follows that casualty period; the page does not name a single closing day. Added in Canadian Batch 2.

name: Operation Blockbuster
notes: II Canadian Corps offensive that began at 04:30 on 26 February with the 2nd Division on the Calcar-Udem ridge (Stacey p. 492) and carried through the Hochwald and Xanten to the end of the fighting west of the Rhine (p. 521). The end date follows the Veritable closing date on p. 522, because Stacey names no separate end for Blockbuster. Added in Canadian Batch 2.

name: Operation Tractable
notes: First Canadian Army daylight attack towards Falaise, first called Tallulah and renamed Tractable on 13 August (Stacey p. 236); launched at noon on 14 August (Ellis, vol. I, p. 430; Stacey pp. 238-241). The end date 21 August is the day the Falaise Gap was finally closed (Stacey p. 264; Ellis, vol. I, pp. 447-449); neither history gives a separate end day for Tractable, so the end follows the Gap and is an inferred value. Added in British Batch 1, as the Canadian Batch 1 deferred item; it sits inside OP-FALAISE (12-21 August).

name: Operation Bluecoat
alt_names: British attack from Caumont; Caumont offensive
notes: Second Army offensive south from the Caumont sector by VIII and XXX Corps, begun on 30 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 386-395, which calls it the British attack at Caumont). The name and the end date 7 August are from the Wikipedia infobox; Ellis describes the fighting to 8 August (pp. 409-411) without naming a closing day. Added in British Batch 1; it belongs to the Northern France campaign (25 July to 14 September).

name: Operation Astonia
notes: I Corps assault on Le Havre (First Canadian Army), called a neat and expeditious three-day operation in the second week of September (Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 331, which gives the name); Ellis, vol. II, pp. 14-15 dates the assault from 17:30 on 10 September to the surrender of the forts on 12 September (the operation is not named in the Ellis text read). Added in British Batch 2 as a deferred British Batch 1 item; it sits inside OP-CAMP-NORTHERN-FRANCE (25 July to 14 September). primary_place_id: old value blank, new value PL0169 (Le Havre); reason: sourced namesake or objective place that appears among this operation's preferred claims (Task 2, OB6, 24 November 2026).

name: Operation Infatuate
notes: The capture of Walcheren: Infatuate I (the amphibious attack on Flushing across the Scheldt) and Infatuate II (the seaborne assault at Westkapelle), launched on 1 November 1944 (Stacey, pp. 379-380 and 407, which give the names; Ellis, vol. II, p. 114, which gives the day). The end date 8 November is the day the last strong-point between Veere and Domburg fell and the only Germans left on the island were prisoners (Ellis, vol. II, p. 123). Added in British Batch 2 as a deferred British Batch 1 item; it is the Walcheren part of OP-SCHELDT (2 October to 8 November) and is linked to it by an operation relation, because the validator prefers a campaign as the parent of an operation.

name: Operation Pheasant
notes: Second Army (XII Corps) and I Corps clearance of North Brabant towards the Maas, after the reorientation of Second Army by the directive of 16 October (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 123-127). The name and the dates 20 October to 4 November are from the Wikipedia infobox; Ellis does not name the operation and dates the XII Corps advance from 22 October and the end of XII Corps task to 5 November (p. 126), and Stacey (the other history read for this batch) does not mention it. Added in British Batch 2 as a deferred British Batch 1 item; the dates are secondary and the only British rows that use it are the two flagged 1944 rows added in this batch.

name: Operation Blackcock
notes: XII Corps (7th Armoured, 52nd and 43rd Divisions) clearing of the triangle between the Roer and the Maas, from the Wurm to Roermond: began at 07:30 on 16 January 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 243) and ended with the German statement of 26 January that the Roer bridgehead no longer existed (p. 246). The name Blackcock is in the Ellis index and chapter heading (pp. 238-246) and in Stacey, p. 450, which says it was completed by 26 January. Added in British Batch 2.

name: Operation Plunder
alt_names: Rhine crossing; Crossing of the Rhine
notes: Twenty-First Army Group assault across the Rhine, Rees to Rheinberg, with Operation Varsity supporting it: the amphibious phase began at 21:00 on 23 March 1945 (Stacey, pp. 530-534, which give the name; Ellis, vol. II, p. 288, which describes the crossing without the code name). The end date 27 March is the last day to which Ellis dates the capture and expansion of the bridgehead (pp. 293-294) and is an inferred value; Ellis gives no closing day. Added in British Batch 2.

name: Western Europe before the Normandy landings
notes: Holding umbrella for positions before 6 June 1944 (decision Scott, 4 November 2026: the dataset may cover the whole war). Start = the sanity bound (1 September 1939), end = the day before the first CMH streamer (Normandy, 6 June 1944). No CMH streamer covers these dates, so the derived campaign label is blank. Replace with proper campaigns when earlier periods are entered.

notes: Per-front holding umbrella for rows outside the Western Front (theater decision Scott, 9 November 2026: keep out-of-theater data, each row with its theater). notes: Per-front holding umbrella for rows outside the Western Front (theater decision Scott, 9 November 2026: keep out-of-theater data, each row with its theater). notes: Per-front holding umbrella for rows outside the Western Front (theater decision Scott, 9 November 2026: keep out-of-theater data, each row with its theater). name: Home front
notes: Per-front holding umbrella for rows outside the Western Front (theater decision Scott, 9 November 2026: keep out-of-theater data, each row with its theater). Added with the two-level theater vocabulary (branch theater-vocabulary, 25 November 2026) so that each theater has a place to file claims that are not yet under a named campaign. date_basis derived. Dates are working bounds: start = 7 July 1937, the global dataset floor; end = 2 September 1945. Existing German rear-area rows stay on theater=home_germany under OP-HOME-GERMANY. New rows for other countries' home establishments may use theater=home_front under this umbrella. No CMH ETO streamer applies, so the derived campaign label is blank.
